author: Einstein
inspection: Each of the seven original durable PNGs was opened separately at original detail; no former figure gate reused or repeated.

sourceFacts: One dark rectangular demonstration backboard in a double frame, with a lower base edge.
Two flexible leads enter from the lower left. One rises to a left upper attachment; the other sweeps across the lower board toward the upper right, with an indistinct terminal.
A faint approximately horizontal wire crosses the board toward a pulley at the right. A small suspended block is below the pulley.
One outlined graduated strip is immediately right of the hanging part. The marks are short, unnumbered and degraded; no voltage, current, temperature, length or mass values are printed.
The current frozen text supplies fixed-end, pulley and hanging load identities; the dark scan does not independently resolve every conductor joint.
hardBlockers: Cannot reliably inventory the exact count/spacing of the ruler strokes from this degraded source PNG.
Second lead terminal and the dark wire/pulley connection are not reliably resolved. No circuit topology or alternative wire-state curve may be invented.
figures.renderingDecision: Source inventory and full context only; native initial drawing deferred, no repair used.

sourceFacts: Upper view: one long metal cradle/base seen obliquely, with two raised end supports and a visible groove in each support. The central channel is empty.
Lower view: one detached long iron rod, approximately parallel to the upper cradle. A short transverse pin passes through the left end; the right end has a screw/wing-nut fitting.
These are two spatially separate apparatus views, not before/after fracture panels. The printed image has no arrows, temperature marks, calibrated dimensions or material labels.
The frozen text identifies the transverse brittle member as cast iron and explains the restrained-cooling demonstration. It does not authorize a newly drawn fracture or assembly step.
modernRegularization: Clean geometric perspective and simplified uncalibrated grooves/fastener outlines; source apparatus arrangement retained.

sourceFacts: One continuous pipe with two horizontal end runs and a single upward rounded expansion loop between them.
Two paired pipe-wall contours enclose the open interior of the loop; no separate disconnected loop or branch.
One dark collar/clamp is on each horizontal run, two clamps total. Both have upper and lower bolt-like projections.
No arrows, temperature states, measured pipe diameter, dimensions, labels or calibrated displacement.
modernRegularization: Smooth continuous pipe-wall geometry and clean clamp outlines; no calibration or additional pipeline branch.

sourceFacts: One straight horizontal bonded two-layer strip. Copper is the upper layer, iron is the lower layer.
Five rivet stations, each with a top and a bottom head, bind both layers. The five stations have corresponding upper/lower positions.
Printed copper label is above the upper layer and iron below the lower layer. Translate only these identities to Cu and Fe.
No applied force arrows, temperature values, strain data or quantitative dimensions.
modernRegularization: Two semantic fill roles distinguish the original materials; clean rivet heads, Latin chemical symbols and straight uniform outlines.

sourceFacts: One bonded two-layer strip bends into an upward arch, with ends lower than its middle.
Copper is the outside/upper longer arc; iron is the inside/lower shorter arc. Their interface is continuous.
Five rivet stations, each with outer and inner heads, span the bonded layers. Keep both heads at each corresponding radial station.
Printed copper identity lies above the middle and iron below. English replacements are Cu and Fe, not a reversed layer assignment.
No calibrated curvature, temperature, force labels or added free unbonded strips.
modernRegularization: Uncalibrated circular-arc construction makes the source outside/inside relationship executable; clean material distinction and matched rivet stations.

sourceFacts: One reinforced-concrete member in oblique perspective; the exposed steel cage is on the left, concrete occupies the right.
Eight transverse rectangular stirrup stations are visible: four in the fully exposed left region and four at the open/cutaway front of the concrete region.
Four longitudinal steel traces follow the four corners of the rectangular cage. Portions are obscured by concrete; no hidden interior rod count can be read from the image.
Three visible hooked/returned bar ends occur at the exposed region: two at the left nearer ends and one near the upper transition to concrete.

The concrete has a plain top and a stippled front, with the front opened around the four right-hand stirrups; the far right is solid concrete. Steel bars continue into this member, not beside an unrelated block.
No dimensions, spacings, load arrows, reinforcement design values or material labels.
sourceFindings: Only visible rods and stirrups are inventoried; no claim about unseen reinforcement behind intact concrete, exact construction specification or physical rod spacing.
modernRegularization: Clean perspective and schematic front cutaway, flat concrete tone replaces scan stipple; visible member counts and material embedding retained.

sourceFacts: One metal sphere is centered above one annular metal ring. The ball overlaps/occludes the ring's rear rim; a crescent of the bore remains visible in front.
The ring is seen obliquely as an ellipse with a through-hole, not as a filled disk, second sphere or flat solid plate.
Ball and ring are a single uncalibrated apparatus view, not three thermal-state panels or a supplied solution about passage.
No handle, support stand, dimension labels, temperature labels, movement arrows or printed quantitative clearance.
modernRegularization: Clean circular ball silhouette and perspective annulus; contrasting semantic material fill only, no thermal-state or pass/fail annotation.
